subject: Social Habits
title: Helping at home and school
objectives: Children will do small helping jobs.
Children will say how they helped.
content: Helping my teacher, helping at home, and our class helpers.
teachingActivities: Give every child a small real job; make jobs safe and short; praise the effort; rotate helpers daily; use a helpers chart; link jobs at school to jobs at home; never compare children.
learnerActivities: Do small helping jobs and say "I helped".
assessment: Observe whether each child does a small job with support and says "I helped".
expectedOutcomes: Does a small job with support.

lessons.title: Helping my teacher
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will do a small helping job for the teacher.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt to listen, say sorry and help a friend.
lessons.starter: Show the helpers chart and say "Today our helpers are Ada and Tunde."
teacherActivities: Show the jobs: line leader, door helper, tidy helper and plant helper.
Choose helpers and give each a job.
Change helpers so everyone has a turn.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show the jobs: line leader, door helper, tidy helper and plant helper. Children: Children look at the jobs.
Step 2. Teacher: Choose helpers and give each a job. Children: Child does their job.
Step 3. Teacher: Say "Thank you, helper." Children: Child says you are welcome.
Step 4. Teacher: Change helpers so everyone has a turn. Children: Another child takes the job.

practical.title: Class helpers
practical.safety: Give only safe jobs and supervise closely. Use child-size tools and never leave children alone with them.

differentiation.support: Do the job together with the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to choose the next helper.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Say thank you to the helpers.
lessons.homeConnection: Give your child a small job to do at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "do a small helping job for the teacher" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: I am a helper, I help every day.

lessons.title: Helping at home
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will name jobs they can do at home.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt to listen, say sorry and help a friend.
resources: Pictures of home jobs: sweeping, washing plates, setting the table, putting away shoes
lessons.starter: Show a picture of a child putting away shoes and say "This child helps at home."
teacherActivities: Show each picture and name the job.
Act out each job with toys.
Ask "What do you do at home?"
learnerActivities: Children look and repeat the job.
Child says or points to a job.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show each picture and name the job. Children: Children look and repeat the job.
Step 2. Teacher: Act out each job with toys. Children: Children act the jobs.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask "What do you do at home?" Children: Child says or points to a job.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "Helping makes our home happy." Children: Children smile and nod.

practical.title: Home jobs
steps: Say what you do at home.
practical.safety: Use plastic dishes and child-size tools only. Never encourage children to touch hot or sharp things at home.

differentiation.support: Act together and say the job.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to name two jobs.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do you do at home?

lessons.homeConnection: Let your child do one small job and say thank you.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "name jobs they can do at home" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Plant helpers
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will help to care for a class plant.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt to listen, say sorry and help a friend.
lessons.starter: Show the class plant and say "Our plant needs a helper. Who will water it?"
teacherActivities: Show how to pour a little water slowly.
Let each helper water the plant.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to pour a little water slowly. Children: Children watch.
Step 2. Teacher: Let each helper water the plant. Children: Child waters the plant.
Step 3. Teacher: Say "Thank you, helper." Children: Children clap and cheer.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "Plants need us." Children: Children repeat the sentence.

practical.title: Water the plant
practical.safety: Use a tray to catch drips and wipe spills at once. Wash hands after touching soil and supervise closely.

differentiation.support: Hold the can together and pour slowly.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say how often the plant needs water.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.homeConnection: Let your child water a plant at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "help to care for a class plant" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Tidy helpers
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will work as helpers to tidy the classroom.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt to listen, say sorry and help a friend.
lessons.starter: Say "Our room is untidy. Tidy helpers, please help."
teacherActivities: Give each child a tidy job.
Sing the tidy song while working.
learnerActivities: Children look at the tidy room.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Give each child a tidy job. Children: Children take jobs.
Step 2. Teacher: Sing the tidy song while working. Children: Children tidy and sing.
Step 3. Teacher: Check the room together. Children: Children look at the tidy room.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "Thank you, tidy helpers." Children: Children say well done.

practical.title: Tidy team
practical.safety: Use child-size tools and supervise closely. Keep walkways clear and never use cleaning chemicals with children.

differentiation.extension: Ask the child to lead the tidy song.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Look at the tidy room and say "Thank you."
lessons.homeConnection: Tidy up together as a family.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "work as helpers to tidy the classroom" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 5 helpers check
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child helps at school.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have learnt to listen, say sorry and help a friend.
lessons.starter: Sing the helper song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: plant, tidy and home jobs.
At each station watch how the child helps.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: plant, tidy and home jobs. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station watch how the child helps. Children: Child helps with a prompt.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Helper stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep floors dry. Use child-size tools only.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use one station.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to teach a friend a job.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: does a small job; names a home job; waters a plant; says I helped.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 5
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say thank you.
lessons.homeConnection: Keep giving small jobs at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child helps at school" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
